comparison: Both evaluations support the transcriptomic profiling data (C1-C4, C85-C86). OpenEval includes C87 (calcineurin/NFAT expression patterns) which peer review addresses separately in R9. Both acknowledge the RNA-seq data quality and pathway enrichment analyses as sound.

Perfect agreement on C6-C8. Both evaluations support the baseline characterization of the larval regeneration model, EdU incorporation assays, and temporal dynamics of beta cell regeneration without any concerns raised.

Divergent evaluations for C9-C13. OpenEval finds the CsA effects on beta cell numbers fully supported. Peer review accepts the phenotypic observations but expresses uncertainty about mechanistic interpretation, noting that 'evidence of the lineage between ductal cells and beta cells remains suggestive' and lacks 'critical lineage tracing results.'

Divergent evaluations for C14-C18. OpenEval supports the neogenesis interpretation based on neurod1+ cell quantification and EdU data. Peer review groups these claims with C9-C13 and expresses the same uncertainty about ductal lineage conclusions, questioning whether the data definitively establish neogenesis from ductal progenitors.

Divergent evaluations for C19-C22. OpenEval supports the conclusion that CaN acts directly in ducts based on duct-specific genetic experiments. Peer review accepts the phenotypic observations but rates as uncertain, specifically questioning the mechanistic conclusion (C22) about direct ductal action due to lack of lineage tracing.

Perfect agreement on C23-C30. Both evaluations support the dose-response experiments, synergistic effects with Notch inhibition, use of multiple calcineurin inhibitors (CsA and FK506), NFAT involvement, and the overall mechanistic model of CaN-Notch interaction.

Divergent evaluations for C31-C36. OpenEval supports the proliferation data and interpretation that EdU+ beta cells provide direct evidence of ductal origin. Peer review does not challenge the proliferation data directly but expresses uncertainty about the lineage interpretation (C34), stating that evidence 'remains suggestive' without lineage tracing.

Divergent evaluations for C37-C41. OpenEval supports the model of CaN acting on Notch-responsive progenitors and the balance between proliferation and differentiation. Peer review acknowledges the proliferation and depletion observations but expresses uncertainty about the mechanistic model (C41) due to lack of definitive lineage tracing.

Perfect agreement on C42-C47. Both evaluations support the adult/juvenile zebrafish data showing transient CsA effects and the necessity of CaN regulation across developmental stages. Reviewers acknowledge this provides 'valuable information regarding molecular mechanisms.'

Perfect agreement on C48-C54. Both evaluations support these background/contextual claims about mammalian beta cell regeneration capacity and ductal progenitor potential as well-established literature-based facts.
Perfect agreement on C55-C63. Both evaluations support these background claims about the zebrafish regeneration model as well-established contextual information supported by appropriate citations.
Perfect agreement on C64-C69. Both evaluations support these background claims about Notch signaling in zebrafish pancreatic progenitors as established knowledge providing necessary context.

Perfect agreement on C70-C73. Both evaluations support these background claims about CaN's role in other regenerative systems and its interaction with Notch signaling as appropriate contextual information.
Perfect agreement on C74-C79. Both evaluations support these background claims about progenitor division modes and their regulation as appropriate mechanistic context.
Perfect agreement on C80-C84. Both evaluations support these background claims about CaN's role in senescence and translational relevance to human diabetes as appropriate contextual information.
